findings.text: Pseudo filesystem superblock setup derives capacity, block geometry, magic, operations, export, xattr, time granularity and dentry flags from caller context, falls back to a minimal statfs only table when no operations are supplied, creates an owner accessible root directory with fresh timestamps, and reports allocation failure as out of memory.
The first inode number is reserved for the pseudo root and later allocations must avoid collision with it through a reservation of one value.
Nodev mount construction accepts a filesystem context plus a fill callback and forwards them to generic super acquisition without device lookup.
Pseudo filesystem context operations expose teardown that releases private context and tree construction that targets the nodev helper.
Simple open propagates the inode private pointer to file private state when present and always reports success.
Linking an existing entry refreshes timestamps on child and parent, raises child link count, pins the child, and attaches the new dentry persistently.
Emptiness testing holds the parent dentry lock while walking children, acquires each child lock with a nested subclass, and reports empty only when no positive child exists.
Directory removal requires an empty victim, drops links on victim and parent, detaches the victim, and marks the dentry discardable.

Rename accepts only no replace and exchange options, delegates the exchange case, rejects a non empty target directory, unlinks an existing target with directory link adjustments, adjusts parent link counts on directory move, and refreshes timestamps of participants.

Memory backed folio input output provides zero filled up to date content on read, obtains a writable folio by page index with zeroing of untouched regions on partial non up to date writes, and on completion zeroes short copy tails, extends size past end, marks dirty, unlocks and releases, returning copied length.
Ram address space operations bind read, write begin and write end handlers with a no operation dirty marker for memory backed files.

Pinned filesystem mount state is guarded by a dedicated spinlock protecting lazy kernel mount creation, reference acquisition and use count changes, with release clearing the stored mount when the count reaches zero under the same lock.

Bounded buffer helpers reject negative offsets, return zero on exhausted range or empty request, truncate length to remaining space, advance the offset by transferred amount, and report fault when user copy makes no progress.
Transactional helper allows at most one writer payload per open, enforces a size ceiling, publishes completed size with ordering, serves reads from stored payload, and frees state on release.
Transaction creation serializes installation of file private state with a static spinlock to enforce single writer busy failure.
Transaction setup fails oversize requests, allocation failure, repeated write, and user copy fault, while completion asserts the size bound.
Small attribute helper state bundles get and set callbacks, paired fixed size text staging areas, an opaque datum, a format selector, and a mutex serializing buffer access.
Attribute file lifecycle allocates helper state, captures inode private datum with format and callbacks, initializes the mutex, disables seeking, and frees the helper on release.

Attribute read and write require a configured callback, take the helper mutex interruptibly, reuse cached formatted output for continued reads, bound input staging with termination, parse as signed or unsigned per entry, and claim full input length on successful store.
Nonseekable open clears seek and positional access mode bits while reporting success.

Thirty two bit file handle encoding uses a two word form for inode plus generation and a four word form adding parent inode plus generation, reporting required length and an invalid marker when the caller buffer is too small.

Handle to dentry resolution validates minimum length, supports both handle flavors through caller supplied inode lookup, and returns an alias, while parent resolution requires a longer handle with parent flavor and tolerates missing parent generation.

Simple fsync waits for the requested file range, skips metadata sync when clean with datasync aware dirty checks, otherwise syncs metadata and folds pending writeback errors, with the full variant additionally issuing a block device cache flush.

Addressability checking rejects overflow of block count shifted by block size bits, accepts an empty filesystem, rejects tiny block sizes, and rejects geometries exceeding sector or page index ranges.
No operation helpers provide always successful fsync, an always invalid direct input output marker whose presence signals direct support, memory release for links, and direct link target retrieval.

Symlink inode operations bind link retrieval, empty directory inode operations bind failing lookup with denied setattr and xattr listing, and empty directory file operations bind constrained seek with generic directory read, dot only iteration and no operation fsync.
An empty directory presents only dot entries, reports missing on lookup, denies attribute changes and extended attribute listing, and limits seekable size to two entries.

Case insensitive dentry comparison prefers exact match, otherwise requires a casefolded parent and stabilizes inline short names against concurrent rename before unicode comparison, while hashing skips non casefolded directories and treats folding failure as invalid only under strict encoding.
Case insensitive dentry operations bind hash and compare with optional encryption revalidation, while the encrypted only variant binds revalidation alone.

Case insensitive directory matching prefers exact match, decrypts names when the parent is encrypted requiring an available key, compares against prefolded or plain query with unicode helpers, reports no match with rate limited logging on invalid encodings under strict mode, and always releases temporary decryption storage.
Strict encoding mode is indicated by a flag bit held in superblock encoding flags.
Short string initializers associate a name pointer with a length for directory entry and crypto name descriptors.
Encrypted inode state is indicated by a flag bit held in inode flags.

Encryption key presence reflects a non null per inode crypto context whose address derives from a superblock provided offset added to the inode base, with a fallback build reporting absent, while filename translation in the observed configuration reports unsupported.

Superblock dentry operation selection prefers the case insensitive table when encoding is present, otherwise the encrypted table when crypto operations are present, leaving defaults unchanged when neither applies.

Attribute access without a configured callback denies access, rename with unsupported flags or a non empty target fails, removal of a non empty directory fails, and unrepresentable geometry surfaces as too big.
